c.tagline: Temple bells, mountain air, and chaos woven into ancient courtyards.

taxi.fareNote: Meters are often 'broken'; agree fare upfront or insist on the meter (bhada) before departing.

emergency.note: Tourist Police: +977-1-4247041; response times and resources are limited outside central areas.

avoid.reason: Fake trekking-guide and "friendly student" scams in Thamel; pickpocketing in crowds; sort trekking permits officially

hood_desc: The backpacker and trekking hub with narrow lanes packed with gear shops, budget guesthouses, bars, and travel agents; suits first-timers, trekkers, and nightlife seekers.
Quiet Tibetan Buddhist quarter centered on the giant whitewashed stupa, ringed by monasteries and thangka shops; suits culture and spirituality-focused travelers wanting a calmer base.
A historic Newari city across the Bagmati river with a UNESCO Durbar Square, artisan courtyards, and boutique cafes; suits culture lovers wanting fewer crowds than central Kathmandu.
Leafy, upscale diplomatic and residential enclave close to the center with embassies and quiet tree-lined streets; suits business travelers and those wanting comfort with easy access.
Central boulevard near the Royal Palace with high-end shops, airlines offices, and legacy luxury hotels; suits travelers wanting a polished, central base.

water.note: Avoid tap water; drink only bottled, filtered, or boiled water.

transit.pay: Cash paid to the conductor on board for most buses and microbuses; Sajha Yatayat has some smart-card pilot routes but cash is standard. No unified fare card exists valley-wide.
transit.hours: Roughly 6am-8pm; little to no night service, so taxis/ride-hailing apps are used after dark.
transit.note: No metro or rail system exists; most visitors rely on taxis, ride-hailing apps, or walking within neighborhoods.

bus: Greenline and tourist coaches to Pokhara/Chitwan
Long-distance buses from Gongabu (New) Bus Park

transit.m: Prepaid taxi counter (fixed fare) to Thamel
Public bus/microbus to Ratna Park (with luggage impractical)

tip.r: 10% is appreciated at restaurants without a service charge; not expected for taxis, though rounding up is common.

landmarks: Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple)
An ancient hilltop stupa with the Buddha's watchful eyes painted on all four sides, offering panoramic views over the Kathmandu Valley.
Boudhanath Stupa
One of the largest spherical stupas in the world and the spiritual heart of Tibetan Buddhism in Nepal, ringed by prayer wheels and colorful prayer flags.
Pashupatinath Temple
A sacred Hindu temple complex on the Bagmati River, one of the holiest Shiva shrines in the world and a vivid scene of ritual and pilgrimage.
Kathmandu Durbar Square
A UNESCO World Heritage plaza of ornate pagoda temples and the historic Hanuman Dhoka royal palace, the ceremonial heart of old Kathmandu.
Patan Durbar Square
An exquisitely preserved square of Newari architecture and intricately carved temples, showcasing some of the finest craftsmanship in the valley.
Bhaktapur Durbar Square
A remarkably preserved medieval city center famed for its pottery square, wood carvings, and the towering Nyatapola Temple.
Kopan Monastery
A hillside Tibetan Buddhist monastery overlooking Kathmandu, known for its peaceful courtyards, murals, and meditation retreats.
Thamel
Kathmandu's vibrant tourist and trekking hub, a maze of narrow lanes packed with colorful shops, prayer flags, and street life.
Garden of Dreams
A serene neoclassical walled garden in the middle of the city, offering a tranquil escape with fountains, pavilions, and manicured lawns.
Nyatapola Temple Bazaar
The lively square at the foot of Nepal's tallest pagoda temple in Bhaktapur, bustling with pottery makers and street life.

train.note: Kathmandu has no railway station and no trains. Nepal's only working railway is the short Jaynagar-Kurtha-Bijalpura-Bardibas line in the southern Terai (crossing from Jaynagar in India), which does not reach the capital. From Kathmandu, travel is by bus or air; to catch an Indian train you cross the border (e.g. at Sunauli or Birgunj) and board on the Indian side.

bus.note: The DTC runs a long, direct AC Delhi-Kathmandu coach; carry your passport as you pass through the Sunauli/Belahiya border. Many other 'Kathmandu to India' services actually take you only to a border town (Sunauli, Birgunj, Kakarbhitta), where you cross on foot and pick up onward Indian transport.

ferry.note: Nepal is landlocked, so there are no ferries of any kind - international or domestic.
